title: How browser HTTP caching works
assumedKnowledge: You can read HTTP request and response headers.

cards.heading: A fresh response can be reused
cards.body: A cache may use a stored response without contacting the origin while it is fresh. Freshness is a permission to reuse, not a promise that the bytes are newest.

cards.heading: Age measures stored time
cards.body: The Age header reports seconds a response has spent in caches. It helps a downstream cache calculate current age alongside time since it stored the response.

cards.heading: Validators name a version
cards.body: An ETag is a validator: a token representing a selected representation. Last-Modified is another validator based on modification time.

cards.heading: Conditional requests avoid bodies
cards.body: A stale cache can send If-None-Match with its ETag. A matching origin response is 304 Not Modified, so the cache retains its stored body and updates metadata.

cards.heading: Directives set the rules
cards.body: Cache-Control: max-age=60 makes a response fresh for 60 seconds. no-store says caches must not store it; it is stronger than merely making it immediately stale.

cards.heading: must-revalidate limits stale reuse
cards.body: Once stale, must-revalidate requires successful validation before reuse. Without it, carefully bounded stale reuse can sometimes be allowed by other rules.

questions.stem: What may a cache do with a fresh response?

options.text: Reuse it without contacting the origin.
Assume it can never be served again.
Always send a conditional request first.
options.feedback: Validation is needed when freshness has ended.

questions.stem: If max-age is 60 seconds, how many seconds is the freshness lifetime?
questions.feedback: max-age expresses the freshness lifetime in seconds.

questions.stem: Which header reports a response's time in caches?
questions.feedback: Age reports seconds spent in caches.

questions.stem: Which conditional request header carries an ETag?

options.feedback: Correct. It compares the stored ETag.
Cache-Control carries directives, not a validator.

questions.stem: What status means the stored representation is still valid after validation?
questions.feedback: 304 Not Modified lets the cache retain its body.

questions.stem: What HTTP status code is Not Modified?

options.feedback: That is the opposite of no-store.
That describes neither no-store nor freshness.

questions.stem: Which directive requires validation before stale reuse?
questions.feedback: must-revalidate prevents serving stale content without successful validation.

questions.stem: For max-age=60, after how many seconds does freshness end?
questions.feedback: The stated freshness lifetime is 60 seconds.
